newsitem.title: HONG KONG: CEF Concord details reorganisation plan.
newsitem.headline: CEF Concord details reorganisation plan.

text.p: CEF Concord Holdings Ltd on Wednesday detailed a proposed reorganisation plan, including a series of asset acquisitions and fund raising actions to buoy the construction and engineering firm.

CEF Concord said it proposed to issue 821.56 million new shares at HK$0.90 each to International Tak Cheung Holdings Ltd (ITC) in exchange for ITC's 35.6 percent interest in Paul Y-ITC Construction Holdings Ltd.
CEF Concord would make a general offer to all the shares, warrants and convertible bonds of Paul Y-ITC group, the company said in a statement.
CEF Concord said it would also acquire from ITC the Unistress group, which makes and markets precast concrete products, for HK$225 million in cash.
It would subscribe for a 51 percent stake in China and Southeast Asia toll road developer and operator CEF Concord Tollways Co Ltd for HK$241.20 million.

CEF Concord also planned to privately place another 500 million new shares at HK$0.90 each with institutional investors, raising a gross HK$450 million to partly fund the acquisitions, the exercise of outstanding put options and early redemption of existing convertible bonds, it said.

The company would also place 280 million 6.5 percent convertible preference shares at HK$1.06 per share to raise a gross HK$297 million to fund the balance of the commitment in the purchases and for working capital purposes.
After the reorganisation, CEF Concord's major shareholder, Fortune Leader Ltd, would hold 8.7 percent of the company, down from 51.4 percent. ITC would have 51.7 percent of the company.
The company also proposed to change its name to Pacific Rim Infrastructure Management Enterprises Ltd.

The reorganisation plan is subject to several conditions included the granting of the waiver by the related authorities of a general offer obligation by ITC for the securities of CEF Concord, it added.
